name: MonarchAiSharedSession
title: AiSharedSession
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow with MonarchAvatarGroup and MonarchButton, androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with androidx.compose.material3.ListItem and androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip for the participant list
summary: The presence and turn-taking bar of an AI conversation shared by several people and agents: who is here, who is typing, whose request is being answered, what waits, and whether you may send.
whenToUse: Above or below the thread of an AI conversation that several people use at once, so everyone sees whose turn it is and what waits.
whenNotToUse: For presence in a document without an assistant use MonarchPresenceAvatars. For the agents of a task without people use MonarchAiMultiAgentRoster.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchAiSharedSession(participants: List<MonarchAiSharedSessionParticipant>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, answering: MonarchAiSharedSessionAnswering? = null, queue: List<MonarchAiSharedSessionRequest> = emptyList(), maxVisible: Int = 4, following: Set<String> = emptySet(), onFollowingChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, queueExpanded: Boolean? = null, onQueueExpandedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, accessRequested: Boolean = false, announcesChanges: Boolean = true, onWithdraw: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onReorder: ((ids: List<String>, move: MonarchAiSharedSessionMove) -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, onInvite: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRequestAccess: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels = MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels())

class MonarchAiSharedSessionParticipant(id: String, name: String, kind: MonarchAiSharedSessionKind = MonarchAiSharedSessionKind.Person, role: MonarchAiSharedSessionRole = MonarchAiSharedSessionRole.Editor, presence: MonarchAiSharedSessionPresence = MonarchAiSharedSessionPresence.Active, activity: MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity? = null, you: Boolean = false, image: Painter? = null)
enum class MonarchAiSharedSessionRole { Owner, Editor, Viewer }
enum class MonarchAiSharedSessionPresence { Active, Idle, Away }
enum class MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity { Typing, Speaking, Reviewing }
class MonarchAiSharedSessionAnswering(participantId: String, forParticipantId: String, label: String? = null)
class MonarchAiSharedSessionRequest(id: String, participantId: String, preview: String)
data class MonarchAiSharedSessionMove(id: String, from: Int, to: Int)

class MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels(label, listTitle, people, agents, agentKind, assistant, someone, quiet, queueTitle, withdraw, remove, moveUp, moveDown, invite, follow, viewerNotice, requestAccess, accessRequested, done: String? = null; here: ((people: Int, agents: Int) -> String)?; showAll, several, queueCount, queueToggle: ((Int) -> String)?; nameWithYou, followLabel: ((String) -> String)?; role, presence, activity: per-enum ((…) -> String)?; activityLine: ((MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity, names: String, count: Int) -> String)?; answering: ((agent: String, requester: String, label: String?) -> String)?; answeringYou: ((agent: String, label: String?) -> String)?; requestAction: ((action: String, requester: String, position: Int) -> String)?; moved: ((requester: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)?, all defaulting to null)

options.name: participants
options.description: Everyone in the session, people and agents, in display order. Mark one person you; their role decides what they can do.

options.name: answering
options.description: The answer in progress: which agent, whose request and an optional short label.

options.name: queue
options.description: Requests waiting for their turn, first in line first.

options.name: maxVisible
options.description: The avatars shown before "+N". At least one; with exactly one too many, all are shown.

options.name: following
options.description: The ids of the people you follow.

options.name: onFollowingChange
options.description: Shows a Follow toggle beside every other person in the list; receives the new set.

options.name: queueExpanded
options.description: Whether the queue is shown, when the app owns it. null lets the Queue button own it.

options.name: onQueueExpandedChange
options.description: Called when the Queue button is pressed, with the new value.

options.name: accessRequested
options.description: Replaces a viewer's Request access button with "Access requested".

options.name: announcesChanges
options.description: Announces status changes and queue moves to TalkBack.

options.name: onWithdraw
options.description: Shows Withdraw on your own requests.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Shows Move up and Move down to an owner; receives the request ids in their new order and the move.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Shows Remove on other people's requests to an owner.

options.name: onInvite
options.description: Shows an Invite button; the app opens its own invite flow.

options.name: onRequestAccess
options.description: Shows Request access in a viewer's notice.

states.name: quiet
states.description: "No requests in progress" in the subtle text color.

states.name: answering
states.description: The answering agent's avatar ring turns (still when animations are removed) and the status starts with whose request it answers, "your request" when it is yours.

states.name: activity
states.description: Other people typing, speaking or reviewing are named, two at most, else counted; your own activity is left out.

states.name: queue
states.description: "Queue (2)" shows or hides the waiting requests; your own requests are on the subtle AI fill.

states.name: owner
states.description: Move up, Move down and Remove on requests when the callbacks are given; the moves at the ends are disabled.

states.name: viewer
states.description: A notice "You can watch but not send" with Request access, or "Access requested".

states.name: empty
states.description: No avatars; only the status line.

appearance: The status line is caption text in the default role (subtle when quiet). The viewer notice is on the muted fill; your requests on the subtle AI fill with the AI border, others on the subtle fill with the subtle border. Avatars carry presence dots (online, away, offline colors). All colors are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web opens the participant list in a popover; Android presents it in a Material 3 ModalBottomSheet, as iOS uses a sheet, and the whole stack is one button because overlapping avatars are too small to tap. Follow toggles are Material 3 FilterChips with a selected state. The web throttles announcements with announceInterval; as on iOS, each change of the announced clauses is announced, and typing and speaking never are. Follows are a hoisted Set with onFollowingChange instead of following, defaultFollowing and onFollowChange; the queue's open state is optionally hoisted with queueExpanded and onQueueExpandedChange; the list's open state is internal. The Queue button has expand and collapse actions, so TalkBack reads its expanded state. Presence is the avatar's presence dot (active online, idle away, away offline) and always written in the list. The web restores keyboard focus after a queue action; Compose does not move focus, the move is announced instead. The web passes a locale for numbers and lists of names; Android uses string resources. The parity map listed presence-avatars; as on iOS this bar uses MonarchAvatarGroup directly because it mixes people and agents. Marked experimental because it is a domain composite that no Rook app has adopted yet.
accessibility: The bar is a traversal group named "Shared session".
The avatar stack is one button read as "2 people and 1 agent here" with every visible participant's name, role or "AI agent", presence and activity; its click label is "Show all 3 participants".

In the list each participant row is merged into one element with name, "(you)", role, presence and what they are doing; Follow toggles are separate, named "Follow Sam Lee" and selected while following.
Changes of who is being answered, of who is reviewing and of the queue length are announced through a polite live region; typing and speaking are not, and neither is the first status.
Queue buttons are named with the request, for example "Move up: request 2, from Sam Lee"; a move made here is announced with the new position.
Every button has a 48dp touch target; text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: An answering agent or requester missing from participants is named "Assistant" or "Someone".
More than two people with the same activity are counted ("3 people are typing…").
Without a participant marked you nobody can manage the queue and no viewer notice is shown.
Queue buttons appear only when their callback is given.
